sections.name: Hook
lines: gd_hook
In one night, two fake police officers stole half a billion dollars of art. Today, the empty frames still hang on the wall.
gd_title
This is the Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum heist.

sections.name: The knock
lines: gd_door
Boston, March 18th, 1990. Early in the morning, after Saint Patrick's Day. Two men in police uniforms buzz the museum's side door.
gd_guard
They tell the young night guard they're answering a disturbance call. He breaks the rules, and lets them in.

sections.name: The theft
lines: gd_tied
Within minutes, both guards are handcuffed and taped up in the basement. The officers aren't officers at all.
gd_cut
For eighty one minutes, the thieves move through the galleries. They slice paintings straight out of their frames.
gd_list
Thirteen works in all, including Rembrandt's only seascape, and The Concert, by Vermeer.

sections.name: The hunt
lines: gd_reward
The museum offers a ten million dollar reward for information leading to the art's return. Decades of leads. Rumours. Dead ends.

sections.name: Still missing
lines: gd_frames
The museum's founder wanted nothing in her galleries changed. So the empty frames still hang, waiting.
gd_outro
It's one of the biggest art thefts in history, and it's still unsolved. Have you seen these paintings? Follow for more true crime, animated.
